11.0.0.en: Athaliah: the daughter of Ahab and Jezebel, and the only woman who sat on the throne of Judah.

11.0.1.en: Athaliah, the mother of King Ahaziah, was a wicked woman who always counseled her son to do evil, and no wonder, for she was the daughter of Ahab and his wife Jezebel, and she had the bad qualities of her mother Jezebel and, like her, loved evil and the oppression of others. When Jehu killed her son King Ahaziah, she killed her grandchildren, the sons of Ahaziah, and all who remained of the descendants of David, and so she reigned alone over the kingdom of Judah.

11.0.2.en: Athaliah grew up in a corrupt family that fostered evil and worshiped Baal, and no wonder, for her father was Ahab and her mother Jezebel. The home is the first school of every person, in which his inclinations and tendencies are formed. It is a great responsibility on the father and mother toward their children. May they labor to plant spiritual principles and sound conduct before they concern themselves with their children's success and health and all their material affairs.

11.1.0.en: Jehosheba: she was the sister of Ahaziah, the daughter of the former king Jehoram, and the wife of Jehoiada the priest.

11.1.1.en: As for Joash, his aunt Jehosheba rescued him and snatched him from the midst of the slaughter that befell his brothers, and hid him and his nurse in the bedchamber set apart for the priests in the Temple, where her husband lived. For Jehosheba, the sister of King Ahaziah, had freedom of movement within the palace, so she was able to take the child Joash and hide him without anyone noticing, because they were busy killing the children older than he, as his age at the time of his rescue was one year.

11.2.0.en: Joash stayed hidden in the Temple for six years, during which Athaliah was a usurper of the throne of Judah.

11.2.1.en: Here we see God's providence preserving a descendant of David, Joash, as He promised. But in the kingdom of Israel the royal line did not remain on the throne, because they were wicked, and even if they reigned it was only for a time, whereas the descendants of David endure not only for the whole life of the kingdom of Judah but forever in the person of Christ.

11.2.2.en: Jehoiada endured many dangers to preserve the son of David. We, in the present times, which are surrounded by many dangers, must bear sufferings while preserving the teachings and principles that the Son of David, Jesus Christ our Lord, gave us.

11.3.s.en: (2) Joash is proclaimed king over Judah

11.3.0.en: Jehoiada: high priest in the days of Ahaziah, Athaliah and Joash, and the husband of Jehosheba, the sister of Ahaziah and the aunt of Joash.

11.3.1.en: The executioners: a rank of officers.

11.3.2.en: The guard (runners): they were of the royal guard and carried royal messages on foot, so they were distinguished by speed and strength.

11.3.3.en: Jehoiada was the high priest, a devout man of strong personality, displeased with Athaliah's usurpation of the throne and her evil conduct in the worship of idols. So after the child Joash grew up and was seven years old, that is, after six years of his hiding in the Temple with Jehoiada, Jehoiada sent and summoned the senior officers of the army, who were five, as the book of Chronicles tells us (2 Chr 23:1). After Jehoiada made sure of their rejection of Athaliah's reign and her evils, he informed them that the true king, the son of Ahaziah, was still alive and showed them the child Joash. They rejoiced greatly and made a covenant before God in the Temple with Jehoiada to reform conditions in the country and restore the kingship to the descendants of David, as the Lord commanded, and to depose Athaliah from the kingship. All this was done in complete secrecy inside the Temple, and Jehoiada agreed with them to report this matter to the heads of the fathers and the Levites in all the kingdom of Judah, as the book of Chronicles tells us (2 Chr 23:2, 3) that these five chiefs went to the cities of the kingdom of Judah and gathered the heads of the fathers and the Levites and brought them to Jerusalem, and they made a covenant before God with the king and the high priest Jehoiada to make the child Joash king and depose Athaliah.

11.3.4.en: Jehoiada was patient for six years in which his prayers rose, and God guided him to a plan to set matters right and restore the kingship to the house of David, by making Joash king. So be persevering in your striving, and do not be hasty for results and spiritual fruits; raise many prayers before God, but trust that God cares about your prayers and your striving, and in the end He will surely crown your striving with success.

11.4.0.en: Under God's guidance Jehoiada made a plan to make Joash king, which included dividing the guards into three companies. The first company, that is, the third, guards King Joash, who is inside the house of the Lord, and Joash is to be installed as king on the Sabbath, for important reasons:

11.4.1.en: 1- This is the day of the Lord, holy to Him, so it is fitting to install the king on it.

11.4.2.en: 2- Large numbers worship God on this day in the Temple and the rest of the people in their homes, and no work is done in the royal palace or anywhere, in sanctification of the day of the Lord; that is, the atmosphere is quiet, so Queen Athaliah is taken by surprise by the installation of the true king Joash and finds no opportunity to call on her guards for help, because everyone is sanctifying the day of the Lord.

11.4.3.en: 3- On the Sabbath the courses of the Levites and priests change, so he can use both courses, the first, which has finished its service, and the second, which is about to begin, and so he has a larger number of priests and Levites under him to guard the new king and take part in installing him as king.

11.5.0.en: Of the remaining two thirds of the guards, one stands outside the gate of Sur, which is one of the gates of the Temple and is called the gate of the foundation in (2 Chr 23:5), to repel any attack that Athaliah might try to make. The last third of the guards stands behind this gate, hidden, to help the guards who are outside in the event of any attack. It appears that the second company, which stands outside the gate, was of the guard (runners), that is, the civil guard, and not of the priests and Levites, whereas those inside the house of the Lord guarding the king are of the priests and Levites only, as the book of Chronicles confirms (2 Chr 23:6).

11.6.0.en: In this two courses of the Levites will share in guarding the king, because, as we mentioned, the change of the courses of the Levites and priests takes place on the Sabbath, and so Jehoiada uses the course that has finished its service and the course that is about to begin its service in guarding the new king.

11.7.0.en: Jehoiada commanded that the guards from the Levites be armed and surround the king, and that if anyone else tried to break through their ranks, they should kill him at once; that is, they guard the little king with a strict guard.

11.8.0.en: The five chiefs carried out all that Jehoiada commanded in his well-made plan, and they prepared themselves by dividing themselves in the guard and prepared for the installation of the king.

11.9.1.en: Bucklers (shields): the plural of shield, which is a piece of wood covered with leather with a loop at the back into which the warrior puts his arm, and the shield is used to protect himself from any arrows directed at him.

11.9.2.en: Jehoiada strengthened the Levites with the weapons stored with him in the house of the Lord from the days of David, that is, they became strongly armed to defend the king against any attack. Here we see David's weapons protecting the son of David and his descendant, who is Joash.

11.9.3.en: And David's weapons in the Temple signify the spiritual weapons in the Church, that is, prayer, the sacraments, the Holy Bible ..., which protect a person in his spiritual wars against Satan.

11.10.0.en: The guards surrounded King Joash and the house of the Lord and the bronze altar, from the right and left sides, that is, from the south and north, in a circle, with their faces toward the king in their midst and toward the door of the Temple which is in the east, in readiness to repel any attack.

11.11.0.en: After the guards had taken their stand, each in his place, and the people were filling the outer court of the Temple, because it was the Sabbath, Jehoiada stood and declared to them the evil of Athaliah and her worship of Baal, and this of course distressed all the people present in the house of the Lord to worship the Lord, and that God's command is that the descendants of David should continue on his throne, and that God's providence had kept the son of King Ahaziah alive until this day, and that he was the crown prince and the true king, and not Athaliah, the usurper of the kingship. The people rejoiced greatly where they stood. Then Jehoiada brought out to them the child Joash from the priests' bedchamber and set him in the midst, and put the crown of the king on his head and put in his hand a copy of the law of Moses, as the Law commanded in the book of Deuteronomy, so that the king might keep it in his reign (Deut 17:18-20), and poured on his head the oil of anointing, that is, anointed him king. Then all who stood there clapped their hands and cried out with a loud voice, "God save the king." Thus the proclamation and installation of Joash as king over Judah was completed.

11.12.0.en: While Queen Athaliah was sitting in her royal palace, which is next to the Temple, she heard the sound of loud shouting, "God save the king," and she wondered greatly and asked those around her of the guards, and made sure that everyone heard shouting. So she hurried herself to understand what this gathering and shouting in the Temple was, and she went down herself to the Temple, and perhaps a few guards were with her. She was surprised by huge numbers of Levites and people and saw for herself the child Joash wearing the king's crown with the guard around him, and she saw the guard (runners) outside the Temple, and she went in and saw for herself that a king had been installed in her place. Perhaps this was Athaliah's first visit to the Temple of the house of God, because she worshiped Baal, and at the same time it was her last visit, because she was killed after that.

11.13.0.en: She rent her clothes: a sign of intense grief and despair, and an ancient Eastern custom that remains until now.

11.13.1.en: There she saw the king standing by the pillar, according to the custom followed at the anointing of a new king, with the army commanders and the senior elders around him, and the trumpeters beside him, and all the people in great joy. Athaliah understood that this was an overthrow of the government, so she rent her clothes, crying out, "Treason, Treason." Athaliah forgot that she was the one who began the treason when she killed her grandchildren to usurp the kingship, and what a man sows, that he also reaps; for her helpers and her people betrayed her and restored the right order by making a descendant of David king, that is, King Joash.

11.14.0.en: Jehoiada commanded the chiefs with him of the army commanders to take Athaliah outside the walls of the house of the Lord, so that she would not be killed within it and would not disturb this great celebration of the installation of the new king, and if any of the personal guards tried to guard her, he was to be killed at once, so that the rest would be afraid. Thus she goes out alone and is killed outside. In this Joash reigns in peace and does not share in the shedding of blood, and the people complete their joy, while the traitor is killed outside.

11.15.0.en: The Horse Gate: one of the gates of the city next to the royal palace.

11.15.1.en: The army commanders at once seized Queen Athaliah and took her out from among the ranks of the people and the Levites and headed for the gate of Jerusalem nearest to the Temple and the king's palace, which is the Horse Gate, and they killed her there in front of her palace, and no one paid attention to her, because the people hated her for her evil, and they were relieved of her, to begin a new life in peace with God under the rule of the house of David.

11.15.2.en: This is the end of the wicked. May we take warning and not persist in our evils, because what awaits us is not only earthly chastisement but rather eternal destruction. However persuasive and attractive sin may be, keep away from it as long as it is against God's commandment.

11.15.3.en: If we compare what King Jehu did with Jehoiada's plan for installing the king, we find the following:

11.15.4.en: 1- Jehu became king by destroying many people with violence and brutality, whereas Jehoiada made Joash king in peace, and only Athaliah, the wicked queen, was killed.

11.15.5.en: 2- Jehu removed the worship of Baal and left the other idolatrous worship, whereas Jehoiada, as we shall see, removed all idolatrous worship at the beginning of the new king's reign.

11.15.6.en: 3- Jehu needed deceit and lying to kill the prophets of Baal, because his plan was human, whereas Jehoiada, because he was a spiritual man, had a plan for installing the king without any lie, and he destroyed the idols with all force and relied on the Law, which he gave to the new king, and the covenant with God made by the chiefs, the Levites and the people to worship Him alone.

11.15.7.en: 4- All the people were in fear and alarm of Jehu at his accession, whereas at the accession of Joash there was a great, majestic and joyful celebration inside the house of the Lord, and peace prevailed afterward among all the people.

11.15.8.en: Athaliah had to die at the beginning of the reign of the new king Joash. In the same way sin must die when your life with Christ begins. As happens in the sacrament of Baptism, when the nature inclined to evil dies and the nature inclined to good begins, so in the sacrament of confession it is necessary that you cut off sin and die to it, in order to begin a pure new life with Christ.

11.16.s.en: (4) Jehoiada makes a covenant between God and the king and the people

11.16.0.en: After the installation of the new king Joash and the removal of Athaliah, the usurper of the throne, and after the kingdom was settled and peace prevailed, Jehoiada, who was the true leader of the kingdom and to whom King Joash, the child king, owed submission and honor, took care to make a covenant between the king and the people on the one hand and God on the other, that they would keep His commandments and His worship, and so receive all care and providence from God. Then he made another covenant between the king and the people, that the king would take care to look after his people and serve them, and the people would submit to the king and obey him and warn him if he erred. We notice that Jehoiada cared first of all about the relationship with God, and then about ordering the relationship within the kingdom between the king and the people.

11.17.0.en: Mattan: he was the chief priest of Baal.

11.17.1.en: The members of the assembled crowd gathered and went to the temple of Baal and tore down his altars and broke his images and killed Mattan, the priest of Baal, before the altar, and Jehoiada appointed overseers to take care of ordering the worship in the temple of God, because it had been neglected in the days of Athaliah, the Levites had scattered in the land and the people had departed from worship. But after the covenant with God to worship Him and the tearing down of the altars of Baal, they returned to the worship of God. This is the second work that Jehoiada did, that is, after the covenant to worship God, the worship of idols must be got rid of; and the third work was to care for worship in the house of the Lord, that is, he appointed officers over the house of the Lord.

11.17.2.en: If you want to begin anew with God, then, besides renewing a steady relationship and spiritual practices, you must get rid of all the things connected with evil that you have, that is, everything that causes you to stumble, of friends, pictures, books and places, and keep away from all sources of evil.

11.18.0.en: Jehoiada took with him the commanders of the companies and the commanders of the guard and the representatives of the people who were present there, and they brought the king out of the Temple and went with him in a festive procession, by way of the gate of the guard to the palace, where they seated him on the throne. This is Jehoiada's fourth work, that is, the celebration of the king's sitting on his throne in his palace. It is beautiful to see the people following Jehoiada and sharing with him in his works; that is, God gave him grace in their eyes and he became the spiritual and civil leader of the kingdom, which helped the return of the people to God and the Lord's pleasure with them.

11.19.0.en: Jehoash: the short form of this name is Joash, so the two names are of one person.

11.19.1.en: Joy spread to all the people, and tranquility prevailed in the city after the killing of Athaliah. Joash was seven years old when he ascended the throne.

11.19.2.en: Joash's circumstances seem hard, when he lost his father and all his family and his palace, in which he could have been brought up, and he was at that time one year old. He lived hidden, moving only within narrow limits in a single room. But God's providence allowed these sufferings so that he would keep away from the evil and idol worship that fill the royal palace, and be brought up inside the Temple and love God, and so be prepared for the greatest position in the kingdom, that is, to become a king who worships God. So do not be alarmed by the hard circumstances that you pass through, for they are your way to success and the Kingdom.
